sections.h2: Can I sell my house fast in Port Arthur, TX?
sections.html:
Yes. Port Arthur owners can sell to a cash buyer, list with an agent, or sell as-is, and storm-damaged or inherited houses are common reasons to choose a direct sale. The city is a Gulf Coast port in Jefferson County, and its housing stock has a long hurricane history.

A cash sale skips the lender's appraisal and repair requests, which matters when a house has old damage, deferred upkeep or title questions. A listing may bring a higher price when the house is in good order and you can wait for a mortgage buyer.

  • Sell for cash when repairs, liens, tenants or probate are slowing a listing.
  • List with an agent when the house is sound and you have time.
  • Ask each buyer to put the offer, the closing date and all costs in writing.

sections.h2: What shaped Port Arthur and its neighborhoods?
sections.html:
Railroad pioneer Arthur E. Stilwell began settling the city in 1895, and the city dates its official start to incorporation in 1898. The port opened to seagoing ships in August 1899 after a canal was cut along the western edge of Sabine Lake to deep water at Sabine Pass.

The Lucas Gusher at Spindletop in 1901 turned Port Arthur into a refining center. The city says Gulf Oil set up refining in 1901 and Texaco in 1902, and that by 1957 Port Arthur was known as the center of the world's oil refining.

The city is also a patchwork of older communities. Griffing Park, Pear Ridge and Lakeview were folded in over the years and their names are still used, while Sabine Pass and Port Acres are often treated as separate communities. Sabine Pass has its own school district, water district, port authority and ZIP code. Nearby Jefferson County towns include Nederland, Port Neches and Groves.

sections.h2: How did Hurricane Harvey affect Port Arthur housing?
sections.html:
It hit the housing stock hard. A City of Port Arthur housing solicitation says FEMA estimated that 80% of the city's housing stock was damaged or destroyed in August 2017.

The same document describes federal and state recovery money, including HUD community development funds and state disaster funds, being used for buyouts, rehabilitation and new construction. It also set a goal of 250 new homes by August 2020.

For a seller, that history has practical effects. Buyers and insurers ask about flood history, repairs and permits, so gather what you have: repair receipts, contractor invoices and any flood claim records. If you received disaster assistance, ask the program office whether any recorded conditions travel with the property before you sell.

sections.h2: How do Jefferson County property taxes work when I sell in Port Arthur?
sections.html:
Texas has no state property tax, so local units bill you. The Comptroller says appraisal districts value property as of January 1 and that the tax lien attaches that day, so a buyer inherits any unpaid balance unless it is paid at closing.

Bills are mailed around October 1. They are delinquent after January 31, when a six percent penalty and one percent interest are added, and a collection attorney can add up to 20 percent. Most protests are due by May 15 or 30 days after the notice, whichever is later.

  • Homestead: school districts give $140,000 off the value of a principal residence.
  • Age 65 or older or disabled: an added $60,000, plus a school tax ceiling.
  • Disabled veterans: partial exemptions of $5,000 to $12,000 depending on rating, and a full exemption at 100 percent.

Ask the Jefferson County tax office for a payoff before you sign a sales contract.

sections.h2: What are the deed and recording steps in Port Arthur?
sections.html:
The deed goes to the county clerk where the land sits. A small part of the city extends into Orange County, according to the city's housing solicitation, so confirm your parcel's county with your title company before recording.

The state county clerk manual says a deed must be signed and acknowledged before a notary or other authorized officer to be recorded. Fees run $5.00 for the first page and $4.00 for each added page, plus records management, archive and technology fees. A missing grantee mailing address can add $25.

If a deed was never recorded for an inherited house, the heirs may need an executor's deed, a muniment of title order, a transfer on death deed record or an affidavit of heirship, depending on how the estate is handled.

sections.h2: What if my Port Arthur house has foreclosure, probate or tax problems?
sections.html:
Each has a deadline. A borrower in a Texas non-judicial foreclosure can reinstate by paying the past-due amount within 20 days of the notice of default, and the notice of sale comes at least 21 days before a first-Tuesday auction.

After a sale, the lender must file any deficiency suit within two years, and former owners have two years to claim surplus from a tax foreclosure. A will can generally be probated within four years of death, and a small estate affidavit may fit an estate of $75,000 or less, not counting the homestead.

  • Hurricane-damaged house: sell as-is if repairs would cost more than the value they add.
  • Back taxes: ask the tax office about a payment plan, available up to 36 months at some collectors for a homestead.
  • Inherited house: confirm who has authority to sell before accepting an offer.

faqs.q: Can I sell a hurricane-damaged house in Port Arthur as-is?
faqs.a: Yes. Many buyers purchase damaged houses without repairs. Expect questions about flood history and permits, and gather repair receipts, claim records and any recovery program paperwork before you talk to buyers.

faqs.q: Which county records a Port Arthur deed?
faqs.a: Most of the city is in Jefferson County, but the city says a small portion extends into Orange County. Confirm your parcel's county with the title company before the deed is prepared.

faqs.q: When are Port Arthur property taxes delinquent?
faqs.a: After January 31. A six percent penalty and one percent interest are added on February 1 under Comptroller rules, and the penalty keeps rising monthly until July 1.

faqs.q: How long can heirs wait to probate a will in Texas?
faqs.a: Generally four years from death, though a court can accept a later filing for an acceptable reason. A small estate affidavit is a separate route for estates of $75,000 or less excluding the homestead.

faqs.q: Is Sabine Pass part of Port Arthur?
faqs.a: The city lists it among communities it incorporated, but says Sabine Pass is often seen as separate and has its own school district, water district, port authority and ZIP code. Check which taxing units serve your address.
